name: standard_subscription_recognition
text: RevLens accounts for a standard hosted subscription as a single performance obligation. Access to the Platform, product updates, and standard support are provided together as one combined offering and are not separated into multiple performance obligations, because they are not separately priced or separately purchasable and serve to maintain a current, supported subscription. Subscription fees are recognized ratably (straight-line) over the subscription term, beginning when access is provisioned.

name: onboarding_default_non_distinct
text: RevLens treats implementation, configuration, data-migration, and setup services as not distinct from the subscription by default, and combines them into the single subscription performance obligation recognized over the service period. This default applies whenever the services are configured to the customer's environment or the customer's production access is conditioned on their completion. Onboarding fees are not recognized when billed or when the work is completed; they are recognized over the subscription term together with the subscription.

name: onboarding_distinct_exception
text: Onboarding or related services are treated as a distinct, separate performance obligation only when they are standardized, optional, and available to the customer from third parties (or capable of being performed by the customer), and the customer's access to the Platform does not depend on RevLens performing them. Where these conditions are met and documented, the service is a separate performance obligation and the transaction price allocated to it is recognized at the point the service is delivered and accepted.

name: usage_and_overage_fees
text: RevLens accounts for usage- and consumption-based fees (including per-transaction overage above an included allotment) as variable consideration within the subscription performance obligation. Where RevLens has the right to invoice the customer for usage as it occurs, it applies the right-to-invoice practical expedient and recognizes usage revenue in the amount it is entitled to invoice for each period's actual metered usage, rather than estimating total usage in advance.

name: minimum_commitments
topic: Minimum commitment — floor fixed, excess variable
text: For arrangements with a minimum (committed) fee plus usage above an included volume, RevLens recognizes the committed minimum as fixed consideration ratably over the term, and accounts for usage above the included volume as variable consideration recognized as the usage occurs. The committed minimum is recognized regardless of whether the customer's actual usage reaches the included volume.

name: pure_usage_estimation_constraint
text: Where an arrangement has no fixed or minimum fee and consideration depends entirely on usage, RevLens estimates variable consideration using the expected-value or most-likely-amount method and recognizes revenue as the usage occurs. RevLens constrains the estimate, recognizing only the amount it is highly probable will not reverse, and applies additional caution where usage is volatile, seasonal, or supported by limited history.

name: usage_royalty_licensed_ip
text: Where variable fees are charged for the customer's use of a license to RevLens's proprietary intellectual property (for example, RevLens's analytics library), RevLens applies the sales- and usage-based royalty exception and recognizes the royalty at the later of when the usage occurs or when the related performance obligation is satisfied. This treatment is distinguished from ordinary platform usage fees by the presence of a license of RevLens intellectual property.

name: discount_allocation
topic: Discount allocation — pro-rata default vs directed
text: When a contract bundles multiple performance obligations at a combined price below the sum of their standalone selling prices, RevLens allocates the discount proportionately across all performance obligations based on relative standalone selling prices by default. RevLens allocates a discount entirely to a specific performance obligation only where it has observable evidence that the discount relates solely to that item — namely, RevLens regularly sells each item separately and regularly sells the discounted item on its own at a comparable discount.

name: ssp_and_residual
text: RevLens allocates the transaction price using observable standalone selling prices where available. Where a component's standalone selling price is not observable because it is sold at widely varying prices or has not been established, RevLens estimates it using the residual approach — the total transaction price less the observable standalone selling prices of the other components — provided at least one component has an observable standalone price.

name: material_rights_renewals
text: RevLens evaluates renewal options and future-purchase options for material rights. Where a contract entitles the customer to renew or purchase additional services at a price significantly below the price offered to comparable customers, RevLens treats the option as a separate performance obligation, allocates a portion of the transaction price to it, and recognizes that amount when the option is exercised or expires.

name: nonrefundable_upfront_fees_policy
text: RevLens assesses nonrefundable upfront fees (such as activation or setup fees) for whether they relate to a distinct good or service. Where they do not, they are treated as advance payment for future services and recognized over the period those services are provided. Where such a fee is not charged again on renewal, RevLens evaluates whether it gives rise to a material right and, if so, allocates a portion of the fee to that right.

name: billing_timing_balances
topic: Billing timing — deferred revenue vs contract asset
text: RevLens records a contract liability (deferred revenue) when a customer is billed or pays in advance of performance, and releases it to revenue as the subscription is delivered. Where RevLens performs in advance of its right to bill — for example, where fees are billed monthly in arrears — it records a contract asset rather than deferred revenue until its right to payment becomes unconditional.

name: proration_partial_periods
text: Where a subscription term begins or ends mid-period, RevLens prorates revenue for the partial first or last month based on the number of days of access in that month, and recognizes full monthly amounts for complete months. Proration affects the timing pattern only and does not change the total transaction price or the recognition method.

name: significant_financing_component
text: RevLens does not assess a significant financing component for arrangements with a term of twelve months or less, consistent with the practical expedient for advance payments. For multi-year arrangements involving prepayment of more than one year, RevLens evaluates whether a significant financing component exists and concludes it is not significant unless the timing and rate are clearly material; any adjustment is documented and approved by the revenue manager.

name: contract_validity_collectibility
text: RevLens recognizes revenue only when a valid contract exists: the parties have approved it, rights and payment terms are identifiable, and collection of substantially all consideration is probable. Where payment terms are left to be agreed, cancellation terms are absent, or collectibility is doubtful (for example, a newly formed customer with no payment history), RevLens does not recognize revenue and escalates the arrangement for review.

name: free_promotional_periods
text: Where RevLens provides additional access at no charge as part of a promotion (for example, additional months beyond the billed period), it recognizes the total transaction price ratably over the entire access period, including the free portion. The free period is reflected as a reduction in the monthly recognition rate, not as a period of zero revenue.
